prompt: Build a single-file terminal snake game in Python. Save it to snake.py. Use the curses module from the standard library — no external dependencies. Requirements: arrow keys (or WASD) for direction, snake grows by one when it eats food, game ends on wall OR self collision, food never spawns on the snake body, the direction cannot immediately reverse (pressing left while moving right is ignored), display the current score in a status line, press q to quit cleanly. The terminal must be restored to a usable state on exit.
expected_raw_failure: raw 9B reliably trips at least one of: direction-reversal bug (instant death), food on snake body, snake doesn't grow on food, missing curses.wrapper so terminal stays broken on crash, input() blocking instead of getch nodelay
expected_v3_repair: V3's sandbox verifies imports + curses setup compiles; PR-CoT catches direction-reversal because raw 9B's standard implementation is well-known to have it
notes: Canonical 9B failure case. Single file, fast feedback, playable comparison.

prompt: Write a Python CLI that takes a directory and outputs a tree view to stdout, similar to the `tree` command. Save to tree.py. Requirements: argparse with a positional directory argument and a `--max-depth N` flag (default 10), uses ├── and └── for branching, sorts entries alphabetically with directories first, gracefully skips files it can't read (permission errors), exits 0 on success and 1 on error.
expected_raw_failure: raw 9B doesn't sort dirs-first, crashes on permission errors, ignores --max-depth, gets box-drawing wrong on last entry
expected_v3_repair: V3 catches the crash via permission test; PR-CoT applies the correct unicode pattern
